title: OD$^3$: Optimization-free Dataset Distillation for Object Detection
claim: Our method beats prior methods and baselines at every compression ratio, and even its smallest budget outperforms the best prior method's largest.
layout: single bubble-line plot, x = compression ratio, y = mAP, bubble size grows with ratio, black arrows with red gap labels, dashed red threshold line, legend top-left
description: A single bubble-and-line chart. The x-axis is dataset compression ratio (0.25%, 0.5%, 1%) and the y-axis is mean average precision, 0 to 30. Four series appear in a legend at top-left: K-Center (gray), Random (pink), DCOD NeurIPS'24 (purple), and OD³ Ours (orange). Each series is a line with circular markers, and marker size grows with compression ratio. The orange line sits clearly above all the others. Black upward arrows between the purple and orange points carry red gap labels of 5.7%, 7.3% and 10.1%. A red dashed horizontal line runs from the smallest orange point across the plot. A bold red caption reads 'Our smallest dataset surpasses all SoTA'. The eye goes first to the large orange bubble at top right and then to the red annotations.
caption: \textbf{Performance Comparison of { \texttt{OD\textsuperscript{3}}} on COCO.} We compare the mAP performance of our method to others with different compression rates. The upper bound is 39.8% on the full dataset.
abstract: Training large neural networks on large-scale datasets requires substantial computational resources, particularly for dense prediction tasks such as object detection. Although dataset distillation (DD) has been proposed to alleviate these demands by synthesizing compact datasets from larger ones, most existing work focuses solely on image classification, leaving the more complex detection setting largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce OD3, a novel optimization-free data distillation framework specifically designed for object detection. Our approach involves two stages: first, a candidate selection process in which object instances are iteratively placed in synthesized images based on their suitable locations, and second, a candidate screening process using a pre-trained observer model to remove low-confidence objects. We perform our data synthesis framework on MS COCO and PASCAL VOC, two popular detection datasets, with compression ratios ranging from 0.25% to 5%. Compared to the prior solely existing dataset distillation method on detection and conventional core set selection methods, OD3 delivers superior accuracy, establishes new state-of-the-art results, surpassing prior best method by more than 14% on COCO mAP50 at a compression ratio of 1.0%. Code is available at: https://github.com/VILA-Lab/OD3.
